steps.title: Programming Foundations for Games
steps.subtitle: C# or C++, OOP and data structures for gameplay code
steps.description: Get fluent in the language your engine uses: C# for Unity (and Godot), C++ for Unreal. You learn OOP and composition, the data structures behind inventories and spawners, how memory and garbage collection affect frame rate, and how to version a game project with Git.

topics.name: C# or C++ fundamentals: types, control flow, functions, and value vs reference types
OOP for gameplay: classes, interfaces, inheritance vs composition and polymorphism
Data structures for games: arrays/lists, dictionaries and hash sets, queues, stacks and Big-O
Memory basics: stack vs heap, pointers/references, smart pointers (C++) and garbage collection (C#)
Events and callbacks: C# delegates/events, UnityEvent or Unreal delegates
Game programming patterns: observer, singleton, command and state
Version control for game projects: Git, an engine .gitignore and Git LFS for large assets

steps.title: Game Math & Physics
steps.subtitle: Vectors, transforms and collisions
steps.description: Games are applied math: vectors move and aim things, matrices and quaternions place and rotate them, and collision tests decide what touches what. You learn the math behind movement, cameras and physics, and how to keep it frame-rate independent with delta time and a fixed timestep.

topics.name: Vectors: addition, length, normalization, dot product and cross product
Angles and interpolation: radians, sin/cos/atan2, lerp and smoothing
Matrices and transforms: translation, rotation, scale, local vs world space
Rotations: Euler angles, gimbal lock and quaternion basics (slerp)
Collision detection: AABB and circle tests, raycasts, broad vs narrow phase, tunneling
Rigidbody physics: velocity, acceleration, forces, gravity, bounce, colliders vs triggers
Delta time and fixed timestep: frame-rate independent movement and integration

steps.title: Game Engines: Unity & Unreal
steps.subtitle: Build playable scenes in a real engine
steps.description: Learn how a professional engine is organised: scenes and levels, GameObjects/Actors built from components, prefabs and Blueprints, the script lifecycle, input and UI. A small, polished playable game in Unity or Unreal is what studios look for in a fresher's portfolio.

topics.name: Scenes/levels, GameObjects/Actors, the component model and Unreal's UCLASS/UPROPERTY macros
Game loop and script lifecycle: Awake, Start, Update, FixedUpdate, LateUpdate / BeginPlay, Tick
Reusable objects: Unity prefabs, Unreal Blueprints, Instantiate/SpawnActor and Destroy
Player input: Unity Input System or Unreal Enhanced Input, action maps and character controllers
Game UI: Unity Canvas/UI Toolkit or Unreal UMG, HUDs, menus and resolution scaling
Timing and flow: coroutines, timers, Time.timeScale and pausing
Scene loading, ScriptableObjects/Data Assets and saving game data (JSON, PlayerPrefs, SaveGame)

steps.title: Graphics, Animation & Audio
steps.subtitle: Make the game look, move and sound right
steps.description: Understand how the GPU turns meshes and sprites into pixels, write basic shaders, set up materials and lighting, and bring characters to life with animation state machines, particles and spatial audio. This is what separates a prototype from a game that feels polished.

topics.name: Rendering pipeline basics: vertices, rasterization, fragments, depth buffer, URP/HDRP
2D graphics: sprites, sprite atlases, tilemaps, sorting layers, parallax and texture filtering
Shader basics: vertex vs fragment shaders, Shader Graph or Material Editor, HLSL/GLSL
Materials and lighting: textures, normal maps, PBR, real-time vs baked lighting
Animation: skeletal rigs, Animator state machines, transitions, blend trees and root motion
Particles and VFX: Unity Particle System/VFX Graph or Unreal Niagara, overdraw
Game audio: sources and listeners, 3D spatial sound, mixers and clip load types

steps.title: Gameplay AI, Optimization & Multiplayer
steps.subtitle: Smart enemies, smooth frame rates, connected players
steps.description: Give enemies believable behaviour with pathfinding, state machines and behaviour trees; profile and optimize to hit your frame budget with pooling, batching and spatial partitioning; and learn how multiplayer games keep players in sync over the network. Finish by building and publishing your game for PC or mobile.

topics.name: Pathfinding: grids and graphs, BFS vs Dijkstra vs A*, heuristics and NavMesh
Gameplay AI: finite state machines, behaviour trees and steering behaviours
Profiling and frame budgets: CPU vs GPU bound, Unity Profiler or Unreal Insights
Optimization: object pooling, draw calls and batching, LOD and culling
Scaling to many entities: spatial partitioning (grids, quadtrees) and data-oriented ECS
Multiplayer: authoritative servers, interpolation, client-side prediction and lag compensation
Builds and publishing: platform settings, Android App Bundles, Google Play, Steam or itch.io
